subject: SLA-backed commit & memory-tilt pricing options for Dedicated pool
messages:
From: Oliver James <oliver.james@orpheus-analytics.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@orpheus-analytics.com
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2026 14:13:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated pool sizing + GPU type tradeoffs (H100/A100/L40S)

Hey Logan —

Thanks again for the demo. Two quick asks as we stitch together the internal business case:

1) For a 1.2M query/month throughput profile (peaks at ~1.5x baseline), what do you recommend for a dedicated pool mix across H100 / A100 / L40S to hit a p95 < 220ms for short-chat workloads and p95 < 350ms for longer-context retrieval?
2) How do you price reserved commits vs credits for burst capacity? The CFO likes predictable $/month commitments but the product team wants headroom for spikes.
3) Are SLA-backed latency guarantees feasible if we pick a mixed fleet? If so, what are the typical pricing concessions?

If you can throw back a simple table (capacity, expected perf/$, recommended commit term) that would be awesome.

—Oliver
Principal Product, Orpheus Analytics

-----
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver James <oliver.james@orpheus-analytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing + GPU type tradeoffs (H100/A100/L40S)

Oliver —

Great questions, and helpful to know the peak factor. High-level answers below; I attached a short modeling sheet that shows the numbers behind the bullet points.

- Recommendation: start with a memory-tilted mixed pool: 40% H100 (latency-sensitive gen/chat), 40% L40S (large-context batching and embedding throughput), 20% A100 (cost hedge and background batch jobs). This gives a balance of p95 latency and perf/$ for both short-chat and retrieval-heavy flows.

- Perf/$: H100 gives best single-request latency per GPU but is ~1.6–2x the hourly rate of A100; L40S sits between but shines on large batch throughput due to memory and NVLink efficiency. See sheet: pool_modeling_v3.xlsx (tab: summary).

- SLA-backed latency: yes, we can offer an SLA for p95 at the pool level if you commit to a 12–36 month reserved capacity and a predictable burst credit band. Typical concession: 10–15% discount on list rates for 12mo commit + 6–12% additional for 36mo/longer; SLA credits are tied to measurable p95 windows and are scoped to the committed pool (not spot/burst).

- Pricing constructs: we offer two primary commit models:
  1) Reserved-hour commit (hourly equivalent units) + monthly billing. Predictable $/month and capacity reservation.
  2) Hybrid credits: smaller baseline commit + prepaid credits for bursts (credits redeem against higher-cost GPU minutes). Credits are flexible but do not count toward SLA capacity unless explicitly allocated.

I'll let Marissa put some sample rate-card numbers in the next message. Quick clarifying q: what fraction of your queries are long-context (>= 8k tokens) vs short-chat? That changes the L40S sizing.

Thanks,
Logan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Oliver James <oliver.james@orpheus-analytics.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing + GPU type tradeoffs (H100/A100/L40S)

Oliver —

Attaching the modeling workbook (pool_modeling_v3.xlsx) and a draft SLA term sheet (proposed_sla_term_v2.pdf). Quick notes below from pricing:

- Base assumptions used in the sheet: 1.2M queries/mo, 60% short-chat (<=512 tokens), 40% long-context (>=8k tokens), 1.5x peak ratio, target p95s as Logan called out.

- Example rate-card (net, pre-negotiation):
  • H100 (hour-equivalent): $14.50/hr
  • L40S (hour-equivalent): $9.75/hr
  • A100 (hour-equivalent): $8.25/hr

- For a 12-month reserved commit sized to meet baseline throughput we see: 12mo commit -> ~18% net discount off list by committing to 24/7 pool equivalents; 36mo -> ~26% net discount. Those discounts translate into an effective $/query in the sheet.

- SLA concession examples: for a 12mo commit we can include a p95 latency guarantee with a financial credit cap (e.g. 5% of monthly bill per failure window, cumulative cap). For 36mo we can tighten the cap and increase discount slightly.

- Bursting: we recommend a small standby of CloudLane-managed burst credits (we partner with CloudLane to provide managed burst capacity at a known premium). If you want us to include that reseller pricing in the commercial, I can loop them in (I cc'd their contact).

Next steps I propose:
  1) Orpheus to confirm long-context fraction and acceptable commit term (12 vs 36mo).
  2) We send a formal commercial with line items (H100/L40S/A100 hours) + SLA appendix.
  3) Procurement to review draft contract; we can enable a DocuSign flow after redlines.

—Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachments: pool_modeling_v3.xlsx (workbook, ~75KB), proposed_sla_term_v2.pdf (PDF, ~28KB)

Procurement —

Quick answers inline:  

1) Early termination: We can provide a phased refund schedule for 12mo commits (refund = prepayment remaining minus a ramp amortization schedule). For a 9–12 month flexible option we propose higher monthly rates (premium ~8–12%) to cover capacity risk; exact numbers in the commercial. We can make detailed schedule available in the SOW.

2) CloudLane burst credits: We can either (a) consolidate on Redwood's invoice (Redwood pays CloudLane, we show a single line item) or (b) have CloudLane invoice Orpheus directly. Option (a) is simpler contractually; we'll propose it unless you prefer otherwise.

3) SLA measurement: Confirmed — SLA uses Redwood Console telemetry (p95 windows by route). We will provide daily CSV exports to Orpheus and a weekly SLA digest. Telemetry access and retention are in the proposed_sla_term_v2.pdf.

Next: Marissa and Priyom will draft the commercial and I will push to DocuSign (link will be the HubSpot/DocuSign items shared above).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if procurement wants to walk the numbers.

Logan
